title: Conectores causales: debido a que, a causa de que

sections.content: Debido a que and a causa de que (both meaning "because," "due to the fact that") are the formal alternatives to porque, common in historical writing that wants to name a structural cause -- a law, a policy, a decades-old pattern -- rather than a simple personal reason. Both take the indicative when the cause is a stated fact. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Debido a que las leyes liberales de privatización habían despojado a muchas comunidades de sus tierras comunales, millones de personas se encontraron trabajando tierras que antes eran suyas.
items.english: Because the liberal privatization laws had stripped many communities of their communal lands, millions of people found themselves working land that had once been their own.

items.spanish: A causa de que este despojo se repitió en prácticamente todos los países, la reivindicación de la tierra se convirtió en la demanda revolucionaria más extendida del continente.
items.english: Because this dispossession repeated in practically every country, the demand for land became the most widespread revolutionary demand on the continent.

items.spanish: En algunos países, este descontento permaneció contenido durante décadas, debido a que los gobiernos combinaban represión selectiva con concesiones menores.
items.english: In some countries, this discontent stayed contained for decades, because governments combined selective repression with minor concessions.

items.spanish: La cuestión agraria fue uno de sus motores centrales, precisamente a causa de que esta tensión llevaba ya décadas acumulándose sin resolverse.
items.english: The agrarian question was one of its central drivers, precisely because this tension had already been building for decades without being resolved.

sections.content: Debido a and a causa de (without que) work directly before a noun -- debido a la crisis -- while debido a que and a causa de que introduce a full clause with its own conjugated verb, as in every example above.
